answer: Reputation ripples outward gradually through recorded honest interactions, like pigment soaking into cloth, dyeing the account's standing layer by layer with each faithful epoch. The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: every agent's influence equals account age multiplied by verified honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero and cannot buy shortcuts. A new account's signal stays weak for weeks regardless of capital, capping the speed at which anyone can manufacture voting weight or spam power.
